payload.rationale: One capability containing existing Issue 60 is the smallest complete executable hierarchy: Goal 59 has one repository outcome and no legitimate parallel work item. Completeness comes from ordered, durable gates inside Issue 60: freeze an exhaustive inventory; disposition and reconcile every unique substantive history without mutation of sources; harden and version one candidate; validate and independently review its exact pushed SHA; merge only that SHA; then let one unambiguous tag-triggered Burrito workflow own immutable publication and verify every artifact. This directly resolves cycle-1 concerns about open-ended discovery, non-deterministic cross-platform evidence, and split release ownership without inventing a runtime target or temporary contract. Central acancelas/bos-mcp Goal 216 is read-only coordination context; all mutations remain in acancelas/symphony.

capabilities.title: Consolidate Symphony and publish one verified immutable release
capabilities.context: Goal 59 is the Symphony repository slice of central BOS Goal 216. Current origin/main is tagged v0.2.1, while numerous local/remote refs encode potentially divergent Symphony histories. The codebase is an Elixir/OTP scheduler with high-value invariants in GameApiTrackerAdapter-only BOS access, host-side credential isolation, repository serialization, live immutable claim reconciliation, process-wide provider circuits, RFC 8785/hash-chained outbox recovery, fail-closed workspace recovery, subprocess reaping, Goal authorization/budgets, exact-candidate reviews and release evidence. The only configured production channel is .github/workflows/burrito-release.yml, producing four Burrito executables and checksums; no server/browser runtime target is configured.
capabilities.expectedOutcome: Every history inside a finite execution-start inventory is integrated or proven equivalent/superseded/excluded with exact evidence and no source destruction; one clean pushed 0.2.2 candidate passes complete exact-SHA validation and risk-adaptive review, merges through the governed PR path, and is published exactly once by the tag-triggered workflow as checksum-verified linux_x86_64, linux_arm64, macos_x86_64 and macos_arm64 artifacts with durable BOS receipts.
scope: Freeze one immutable cutoff ledger covering every Symphony worktree root, local ref, origin ref, ref tip, merge-base/ahead-behind state, dirty/untracked/unreadable state, and unique non-audit commit; record exact discovery commands, timestamp and identities.

Disposition every inventory entry as substantive-integrate, already-equivalent, superseded-with-exact-evidence, duplicate, generated/audit-only, or Goal-excluded; integrate substantive changes through ordinary non-force Git operations while preserving all source refs, worktrees and unrelated state.

Resolve semantic overlap across orchestrator/scheduler/capacity, GameApiTrackerAdapter/claims, provider circuits, outbox/canonical audit recovery, Goal planning/execution, workspace recovery, subprocess cancellation, token telemetry, dashboards/adapters and release paths without weakening AGENTS.md invariants.

Create one clean candidate at the next unused version 0.2.2; make release publication fail closed if tag, release or assets already exist, eliminate asset clobbering, and make the tag-triggered workflow the sole publication owner.
Bind targeted checks, repository gates, independent reviews, evidence, PR, merge, tag, release and artifact verification to exact immutable commit identities through bos-mcp/game-api.
outOfScope: Creating new capabilities or Issues, mutating central Goal 216 or sibling repositories, or unrelated product expansion.
Deleting worktrees, refs, commits, untracked files or unrelated changes; force-push, reset-away, history rewrite or destructive cleanup.
Direct GitHub REST/GraphQL or gh-based Delivery operations outside the repository-owned tag workflow; exposing provider credentials to Codex.
Inventing a daemon, server, browser URL, deployment oracle or rollback target absent from repository and BOS configuration.
Moving/reusing a tag, replacing release assets, bypassing checks, accepting stale-SHA evidence, weakening acceptance criteria or allowing unbounded repairs.
acceptanceCriteria: The durable inventory ledger includes exact commands and accounts for every in-universe worktree/ref/tip and unique non-audit commit at a fixed cutoff; every entry has an evidence-backed disposition and no source state is destroyed.

The exact clean normally-pushed candidate contains version 0.2.2 and a single-owner fail-closed no-clobber release state machine, is upstream-reachable, and passes conflict-targeted tests, applicable specs.check, mandatory cd elixir && mise exec -- mix test, make all/full gates, security/recovery assertions, release workflow tests and exact-owner zero-child scan.

Functional/quality, architecture/security and release-integrity reviews pass on the exact SHA; concurrency/recovery review passes when affected paths require it; visual/browser review is explicitly not applicable unless both UI changes and a configured browser target exist.
The governed PR merges the exact reviewed/evidenced SHA without bypass; merged main, unused immutable tag v0.2.2, workflow run and GitHub Release metadata all identify the same commit.

The tag-triggered workflow alone publishes four platform binaries plus four SHA-256 files; native-runner smoke jobs pass, post-publication hashes recompute correctly, clean-install behavior passes, and all irreversible boundaries have durable BOS receipts.

If a pre-existing canonical runtime target is discovered before publication, execution pauses for a versioned scope decision defining provider identity, probes and rollback rather than inventing a temporary contract.

issues.title: Reconcile, verify and deliver the consolidated Symphony revision
issues.context: Existing GitHub Issue 60 is the sole executable work item. Its statement that histories are already preserved is an input to verify, not an assumption. Durable handoffs are the cutoff inventory ledger, disposition/provenance map, versioned hardened candidate, exact-SHA validation/review/evidence bundle, governed merge receipt, and immutable release verification receipt.
issues.expectedOutcome: Issue 60 completes the ordered path from finite exhaustive history inventory through non-destructive semantic reconciliation, exact-SHA assurance, governed merge, and one tag-triggered immutable 0.2.2 four-platform publication.
scope: Gate 1 — Inventory: execute and record exhaustive worktree/ref/commit discovery at one immutable cutoff, separating audit-only history from product history without discarding either.
Gate 2 — Reconciliation: disposition every ledger entry and integrate every substantive unique change while preserving source state and producing a candidate provenance map.
Gate 3 — Candidate/release hardening: set 0.2.2, prove identity is unused, remove clobber/update behavior, and establish tag workflow as sole release publisher.

Gate 4 — Exact-SHA assurance: normal push, targeted and complete validations, clean/upstream checks, platform workflow evidence, required specialist reviews and EvidenceReport, with no more than two strictly-derived repair cycles.

Gate 5 — Delivery: governed exact-head PR merge, confirm main identity, create the unused tag once, observe the tag workflow publish once, and verify release/artifact/checksum/smoke identity before terminalization.
outOfScope: Assuming a consolidation branch or prior release proves inventory completeness.
New work items, sibling-repository changes, destructive/force operations, unrelated fixes, mutable release assets, manual duplicate publication, invented runtime deployment or acceptance weakening.
acceptanceCriteria: Gate 1 blocks until the ledger contains the discovery command set, cutoff, every worktree/ref/tip, ahead/behind and dirty/unreadable state, and every unique non-audit commit.

Gate 2 blocks until every entry has an exact evidence-backed disposition, every substantive history is integrated/equivalent/superseded, semantic conflicts preserve documented architecture invariants, and all sources remain intact.
Gate 3 blocks until candidate version is unused 0.2.2 and the release state machine rejects pre-existing tag/release/assets, contains no clobber path, and has one publication owner.

Gate 4 blocks until the clean pushed exact SHA is upstream-reachable and all applicable targeted/full checks, native platform smoke evidence, specialist reviews and EvidenceReport pass with zero surviving test-owned OS processes.
Gate 5 cannot start before Gate 4; PR head and merged main must equal the reviewed SHA, tag/workflow/release must bind that SHA, and publication must occur once.

Terminal evidence verifies all four binaries and checksum files, recomputed SHA-256 values, clean-install smoke results and durable BOS receipts; absent UI/server targets are recorded as deterministic not-applicable, not silently omitted.

dependencies.rationale: Only one capability exists. Inside issue-60-reconcile-verify-publish the strict dependency chain is inventory ledger -> disposition-complete reconciliation/provenance -> 0.2.2 release-hardened candidate -> exact-pushed-SHA validation/reviews/evidence -> governed merge -> unused immutable tag -> sole tag-workflow publication -> artifact verification and terminal receipt.

risks.context: Divergent refs/worktrees can contain unique substantive work or dirty state.
risks.mitigation: Finite exhaustive cutoff, exact disposition ledger, preserved sources, non-force operations and fail-closed treatment of dirty/unreadable worktrees.

risks.context: Overlapping histories affect concurrency, recovery, audit and authorization contracts.
risks.mitigation: Provenance mapping, conflict-targeted tests, full gates, exact-SHA architecture/security/concurrency review and at most two strictly-derived repair cycles.

risks.context: Direct provider access or child-visible credentials violates BOS architecture.
risks.mitigation: GameApiTrackerAdapter and bos-mcp/game-api exclusively, host-side secrets, command-policy assertions and security review.

risks.context: Split ownership, tag reuse, clobbered assets or stale evidence could publish the wrong revision.
risks.mitigation: Unused 0.2.2 checks, one tag-workflow owner, fail-closed collision behavior, no clobber and exact-SHA identity verification.

risks.context: Cross-compiled artifacts may build yet fail on native platforms.
risks.mitigation: Four native-runner smoke jobs plus post-publication checksum recomputation and clean-install behavior evidence.

risks.context: No daemon/server/browser production target is configured.
risks.mitigation: Treat the configured immutable Burrito release as production and require a versioned scope decision if a real canonical runtime is discovered.

risks.context: Central Goal 216 and sibling repositories could blur mutation authority.
risks.mitigation: Use central Goal only as read-only context and constrain all changes/receipts to repositoryId=symphony.
